title: 10 Bricks a Day - Day 198 - Tent
uncertainties: Based on video-recognized inventory; placement coordinates corrected by the developer using connector checks.
Hinge angles are approximated at 44.5 degrees. A small ridge gap is retained rather than forcing intersecting roof plates.
Detached video subassemblies are reordered into root-outward placements.
Exact gray shades and curved-slope mold variant remain uncertain.

steps.instruction: Start with the green 6×8 plate. Lay it flat with the eight-stud edge running front to back.
Take one gray 1×2 hinge base. Align its two underside sockets with the highlighted studs on the right side of the green plate, then press down.
Take one gray 2×2 hinge top. Line up its hinge fingers with the base’s pin openings and snap them together. Then tilt the top inward to about 45°. The hinge stays attached while it turns.
Place the second gray hinge base opposite the first. Leave the middle open for the sleeping area. Press its two sockets onto the highlighted studs.
Snap the second 2×2 hinge top into the opposite base. Tilt it toward the middle so the two hinge tops lean toward each other.
Take a tan 4×6 plate. Match its underside sockets to the four studs on the first tilted hinge top. Press straight toward the hinge, following its angle. The six-stud edge runs along the tent.
Take a dark gray 1×6 tile. Align its six sockets with the bottom outer row of studs on the first roof panel. Press it onto that row, with the smooth face outward.
Attach the other tan 4×6 plate to the opposite hinge top. Press along the tilted connection, not vertically. The upper edges form the tent ridge.
Add the second dark gray 1×6 tile along the matching bottom edge of the other roof panel. Keep the smooth face outward.
Place the white curved 2×2 piece on the exposed studs inside the tent opening. Press down to finish the small sleeping area.
